fact_en:
Bakit nakakahawa ang paghikab?

We often yawn when we see someone else yawn, so a yawn can feel like it spreads from person to person.
fact_bis:
Nganong makatakod ang paghaya?

Sagad ta mohaya kung makita nato nga naghaya ang lain, mao nga morag mikaylap kini gikan sa usa ka tawo ngadto sa lain.

findings.note: Question and body use paghaya/mohaya/naghaya for 'yawn' ('Nganong makatakod ang paghaya?'). Cebuano for yawn is 'hikab' (12 corpus uses, incl. this card's own title_bis 'Makatakod nga Hikab'); 'haya' means a corpse lying in state at a wake. Recoverable from the title, so lower confidence — but the corrupted word is in the question a child must answer. Only 2 cards corpus-wide use haya for yawn (this one and ffct-03742).

fact_en:
Bakit dumadagsa ang anay sa ilaw?

At night, swarming termites gather around lights like bulbs or lamp posts — not to eat the light, but because they get confused using it to guide their flight.
fact_bis:
Nganong nagtapok ang anay sa suga?

Sa gabii, magtapok ang naglupad nga anay libot sa suga sama sa bombilya o poste — dili kay gikaon nila kini, kundili nalibog lang sila sa paggiya niini sa ilang paglupad.

findings.note: title_bis 'Anay nga Nabungol sa Sugnod' = 'termites deafened by FIREWOOD' for title_en 'Termites Confused by Lights'. Two swaps: sugnod = firewood/fuel (used that way 100+ times elsewhere in the corpus), not suga (light); and nabungol = went deaf, not 'confused'. Dangerous because termites+firewood is plausible enough for a child to believe the card is about wood, not lamps — the body says suga/nalibog, so the title is the defect.

title_bis: Utot Gikan sa Baktirya sa Tinai
fact_en:
Bakit tayo umuutot?

We pass gas because helpful bacteria in our intestines break down some foods and make gas — when it builds up, the body simply lets it out, and that's normal and healthy.
fact_bis:
Nganong mokutkot ta?

Mokutkot ta kay ang mabuot nga bakterya sa atong tinai magbungkag sa pipila ka pagkaon ug maghimo og gas; kon matigom na kini, ipagawas sa lawas — normal ug himsog ra kini.

findings.note: The Cebuano question is 'Nganong mokutkot ta?' and the answer opens 'Mokutkot ta kay...' for 'Why do we pass gas?'. 'kutkot' means dig/gnaw — all 16 other corpus uses are turtles digging sand, birds probing mud, rats gnawing, molars chewing. A child asked 'why do we dig?' cannot answer the intended question. Note: title_bis does say 'Utot', so it is partially recoverable, but the corruption is in the question itself (cf. the fever card asking about 'tugnaw').

fact_en: Weaver ants are fierce hunters that eat up many of the pesky insects living on a tree.
fact_bis: Ang mga hantik bangis nga mangtutukob nga mokaon sa daghang peste nga insekto sa kahoy.

findings.note: title_en 'Weaver Ants' -> title_bis 'Langgam nga Habol'. In Cebuano langgam = BIRD (habol = blanket), so the title a child sees reads 'blanket bird' on a card about ants. Classic Tagalog false friend carried over from the card's own Tagalog title 'Manghahabong Langgam' (Tagalog langgam = ant). The body says 'Ang mga hantik bangis nga mangtutukob...' and never states that a hantik is an insect/ant, so nothing in the Cebuano corrects the bird. Corpus confirms the split: the same corpus writes ant colonies as hulmigas/hantik ('Reyna sa Hulmigas', 'Mamumuo nga Hulmigas', 'Mga Hulmigas') and uses langgam for birds. Same class as the known iro-on-a-cat-card defect.

fact_en: As a monitor lizard grows, it sheds its old skin to make room for new skin underneath.
fact_bis: Samtang nagdako ang bayawak, magpalit kini og daan nga panit aron makabaton og bag-ong panit.

findings.note: EN: 'As a monitor lizard grows, it sheds its old skin to make room for new skin underneath.' BIS: 'Samtang nagdako ang bayawak, magpalit kini og daan nga panit aron makabaton og bag-ong panit.' In Cebuano palit = BUY (corpus check: 74 bis cards use palit/mopalit/paliton and every ordinary one means buy - mopalit og tambal, mopalit og botelya); shedding is ilis/ukang/mangaliskis, which this same corpus uses correctly in the sibling bark card ffct-01736 ('mangaliskis ang daan nga panit'). The Cebuano literally says the lizard BUYS old skin in order to have new skin. The card's only fact - that it sheds the old skin - is never stated anywhere else on the card, so a Cebuano-only child cannot recover it. Source of the leak is the Tagalog 'nagpapalit ito ng lumang balat' (palit = change in Tagalog, buy in Cebuano).

fact_en:
Why does vision sometimes look blurry?

Vision looks blurry when light doesn't land exactly on the retina but falls in front of it or behind it instead.
fact_bis:
Nganong usahay hanap ang atong panan-aw?

Mahimong hanap ang panan-aw kung ang kahayag dili mahulog sa retina kondili sa atubangan o luyo niini.

findings.note: title_en 'Blurry Vision and Retina' -> title_bis 'Bulong Retina Focus'. Bulong is not blurry in any sense - in this corpus its three other bis occurrences are all whisper ('Bulong Pari', 'Tunog nga Bulong' = Whispering Sound), and in Cebuano it otherwise means a remedy/charm; blurry is hanap/lubog, which this card's own body uses correctly ('Mahimong hanap ang panan-aw kung ang kahayag dili mahulog sa retina...'). Weakest of the five: the body fully restores the fact and the title asserts no false claim, only a wrong word, so this is a title-repair candidate rather than a child-misleads-me defect. Flagging it only because the title is the text the child sees first.

fact_en: Crickets, grasshoppers, and katydids are actually all related — they belong to one big group of jumping insects!
fact_bis: Ang kagang, apan, ug katydid managsoon diay — sakop sila sa usa ka grupo sa mga insekto nga maayong molukso!

findings.note: EN "Crickets, grasshoppers, and katydids are actually all related — one big group of jumping insects". BIS: "Ang kagang, apan, ug katydid managsoon diay — sakop sila sa usa ka grupo sa mga insekto...". `kagang` in Cebuano is a mud/land crab (binisaya.com, Wiktionary), not a cricket (cricket = gangis; the corpus itself uses kuliglig 108x and gangis 2x). The card therefore tells a child a CRAB is an insect related to grasshoppers. Nothing in the card corrects it — title_bis is "Insekto nga Molukso" and never names the cricket. Corpus-wide kagang=cricket appears in ~8 cards (004/009/024/025/032/079/080), so the grep pair is worth running.

fact_en:
What do jellyfish eat?

Jellyfish eat tiny sea animals like plankton and small fish, catching them with their trailing tentacles.
fact_bis:
Unsay gikaon sa dikya?

Ang dikya mokaon og gagmay nga mga mananap sa dagat sama sa plankton ug gagmay nga isda.

findings.note: title_bis "Pagkaon sa Bantol" for EN title "Jellyfish Diet". `bantol` is the tasseled scorpionfish / stonefish (Scorpaenopsis, Synanceia) — a venomous FISH, a different animal entirely. The body correctly uses `dikya`, so the title actively teaches a wrong animal name rather than the fact. Systemic: 10+ jellyfish cards corpus-wide are titled Bantol (ffct-02243 "Tusok sa Bantol", ffct-03530 "Siklo sa Bantol", ffct-04714 "First Aid sa Bantol", ffct-03633/ffct-06358 titled just "Bantol") while bodies say dikya — worth a corpus-wide title sweep (grep must be case-insensitive and must exclude the fruit `santol`).

fact_en:
Why do male crickets sing different songs?

A male cricket has different songs for different jobs — including one that warns other males to stay away from its area!
fact_bis:
Nganong lainlain ang awit sa kagang?

Ang lalaki nga kagang adunay lainlaing awit para sa lainlaing katuyoan — lakip ang usa nga nag-abog sa uban nga lalaki gikan sa iyang dapit!

findings.note: EN "Why do male crickets sing different songs?". BIS asks "Nganong lainlain ang awit sa kagang? / Ang lalaki nga kagang adunay lainlaing awit..." — i.e. "why does the mud crab sing". The body never says kuliglig/gangis; title_bis says "Awit sa Kuliglig", so the card contradicts itself and a Cebuano-only child is left believing crabs sing. Same swap as ffct-01825.

fact_en:
Which ants are most common in a colony?

Worker ants are the most numerous in a colony! There's only one queen but thousands of workers — that's why we see them walking around.
fact_bis:
Kinsay pinakadaghan sa kolonya sa langgam?

Ang mga worker ant ang labing daghan sa kolonya! Usa ra ang reyna, apan liboan ang worker — mao nga sila ang kasagaran natong makita.

findings.note: EN "Which ants are most common in a colony?". BIS asks "Kinsay pinakadaghan sa kolonya sa langgam?" — in Cebuano `langgam` is a BIRD (the same batch uses it correctly for birds 10+ times: ffct-01906 agila, ffct-01916 maya, ffct-01899 "langgam nga mananhi"); `langgam` = ant is the Tagalog sense. The card asks about a bird colony and answers about worker ants and a queen, with no correction anywhere (ants are `hulmigas` elsewhere in this same batch — ffct-01858, ffct-01924). A Cebuano-only child either can't answer the question as asked or concludes langgam means ant.

title_bis: Ubo Gikan sa Pito ka Adlaw
fact_en: A common cold usually goes away on its own in about seven days, even without medicine.
fact_bis: Ang sagad nga sip-on kasagaran maayo ra sa iyang kaugalingon sulod sa pito ka adlaw bisan walay tambal.

findings.note: title_en "Colds Clear in a Week" -> title_bis "UBO Gikan sa Pito ka Adlaw". 'Ubo' is cough, not cold (the body correctly uses 'sip-on', as do 50 other corpus cards), and 'gikan sa pito ka adlaw' drops the clearing-up verb, so the title reads 'cough from seven days'. Lower confidence than the others because the body states the real fact; the defect is confined to the title.

fact_en: You can prevent choking by chewing food well, not eating while playing or running, cutting food small for young kids, and sitting up straight while eating.
fact_bis: Malikayan ang pagkatuk-ok pinaagi sa maayong pagngala sa pagkaon, dili pagkaon samtang nagdula o nagdagan, pagputol og gagmay nga piraso alang sa mga bata, ug paglingkod og tul-id samtang nagkaon.

findings.note: EN "You can prevent choking by chewing food well..." -> BIS "Malikayan ang pagkatuk-ok pinaagi sa maayong PAGNGALA sa pagkaon". 'Ngala' is not chewing; the only ngala* forms anywhere in the corpus are 'pagngalan' = naming, and all 52 chewing cards use nguya / usap / mama. The card's first and most important prevention step reads as 'naming the food well', and nothing else in the Cebuano says chew, so that step is unrecoverable.
